messages:
maria: Heads-up — observed a tenant in Dedicated (org: papertrail) losing steady reserved throughput after a neighbour did a big burst. Console shows 'throttled' but the tenant's reserved quota meter kept dropping. Weird.
ashok: Can you paste the metric graphs? CPU/GPU or just quota token consumption?
maria: Putting snippets. The 'reserved_throughput_used' for papertrail goes from 65% to 5% over ~2m while requests still succeed but with long tails. Meanwhile another tenant spiked and we hit 'tenant_isolation_limit' on the node.
sam: Is that the policy where we evict KV cache owners when isolation is triggered? I thought eviction only affects latency, not reserved throughput counters.
maria: Exactly — eviction should not change reserved throughput numbers. I suspect we have a path where requests are rerouted to fallback instances and the counters on the original pool keep decrementing incorrectly.
jen: @maria can you paste the request ids or logs? Also which rollout/policy variant is active for that cluster? we had the new 'soft-burst' behavior on 2026-09-21.
maria: Request ids: req-9a7fb, req-9a7fc, req-9a7fd. Cluster policy: soft-burst-v2, routing: prefer-local-then-fallback. Logs show a flood of 429s to the burst tenant, but our accounting logs show token debit still on the reserved pool for papertrail.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout soft-burst-v2 on cluster ci-west finished at 1827123000
ashok: That bot timestamp aligns. Likely regression from the soft-burst change: we added request-level fallback which creates a proxy that charges the original route before reroute.
dmitri: I can repro locally if needed. Quick theory: metrics are updated in the request acceptance path before we evaluate routing fallback. If fallback executes, we should either transfer debit or refund. We probably forgot refund for batched/delayed reroutes.
sam: Refunds are messy under batching. We often just let the original pool keep the debit and mark it as 'transferred' which assumes transfer succeeds. If transfer aborted we don't reverse.
jen: This explains customer-visible effect: their console shows quota consumed but actual capacity available was consumed by the burst tenant. Not good.
maria: Customer ticket #5242 complaining about sudden 'throughput debt' and long tails. They asked if Dedicated guarantees isolation.
ashok: We need two short actions: 1) immediate mitigation: disable soft-burst fallback on that cluster to stop double-debit. 2) long term: change accounting to apply debits only after final route decision or make transfer atomic with rollback.
dmitri: For (1) I can roll back the flag in ~10m. For (2) I propose we modify the request lifecycle: move accounting to post-routing commit and add compensating refund metric for current data so we can clean historical spikes.
sam: Counterpoint: moving accounting later could add latency in the common fast path. We should gate by a feature flag and optimize hot path with inline fast commit for local route.
jen: Also we need UI/telemetry changes: Console should show 'active_request_location' and 'charged_pool' columns in per-request traces so support can tell where billing happened vs where it executed.
maria: Agreed. For short-term dashboards, can we create an alert on mismatch: reserved_quota_used > pool_utilization + 20%? That would catch double-billing.
ops-bot: alert-manager: created alert 'dedicated_quota_mismatch' in prod-alerts (severity=P3)
ashok: Nice. For the PR: dmitri, can you include unit tests that simulate a fallback path with batching and assert no net double-debit? Also add an integration test that replays the ticket req-9a7fb series.
dmitri: Yep. I'll open a draft PR titled "fix(accounting): avoid double-debit on routed fallback" and link test replay logs.
sam: One more concern: what about billing? Customers were charged for tokens. If we double-debited in accounting but later refund metric didn't run, ops/billing may already see invoices queued.
jen: I'll ping billing to pause invoice generation for that org until we reconcile. Also need a reconciliation job to detect and refund double-charges.
maria: Can somebody own comms? Support needs a short message to customer: "We saw an accounting anomaly due to a routing change; we've paused the cluster variant, investigating; will follow up with remediation and any billing corrections." Keep it brief.
jen: I can send the initial message and loop in billing + legal.
ashok: Postmortem items: root cause, why fallback changed accounting order, missing tests in batching path, lack of per-request charged_pool telemetry, and add canary to the rollout.
maria: Thanks team. Plan: rollback soft-burst flag in 10m (dmitri), create PR with tests (dmitri + ashok), create alert (ops-bot done), billing pause (jen). Follow-up meeting in 30m.
dmitri: Rolling back now.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag soft-burst-v2 disabled on cluster ci-west at 1827123600
maria: Confirmed throughput stabilized for papertrail. Console shows reserved_throughput back in line. Keeping thread open until the PR lands.
jen: I'll draft customer message and add billing as FYI.
sam: Thanks all. Quick note for RFC: we should formalize 'charged_pool' semantics across Dedicated vs Fallback so future routing features don't break accounting.
maria: Agreed — add to platform RFC backlog.
